title: Asa Vermette vs. An Average Rider - How Much Faster is a DH Pro?

rider_ids.A: Asa Vermette (pro) -- light/white Fox kit, Red Bull-branded helmet, bib #3
rider_ids.B: Charlie (average/amateur rider, host) -- black kit, plain dark helmet

track: Australian national DH track, dry and dusty (Maydena Bike Park, Tasmania)
timestamps_source: verified frame-by-frame (1s-interval contact sheets, kit-color + helmet ID) against the three in-video 'Section N: Asa X.XXs / Charlie X.XXs' stat overlays, which are exact ground truth for each section's timed run

segments.notes: Host narration/intro. Some riding b-roll of host (avg rider) likely. Asa introduced at 0:34.
Asa interview, standing. Not riding footage. Asa mentions gaining time in fast off-camber and quick rock gardens.
Setup: Asa rides top lines, host follows to copy lines. Both seen walking bikes up together 145-148s.

Section 1: rock section, dusty corners, off-camber corner, step entry. Asa 21% faster (10.18s vs 13.08s, exact per in-video overlay). Sub-split verified via kit color/helmet across 1s-interval frames.
Section 2: Asa gaps into rut; host rolls the rock. Asa 48% faster (6.07s vs 9.00s, exact per in-video overlay). Sub-split verified via kit color/helmet.

Section 3: G-out compression. Asa full speed, no brakes, holds compression. Host brakes harder -> bigger compression at lower speed. Asa 28% faster (10.28s vs 13.19s, exact per in-video overlay). BEST SECTION FOR SUSPENSION KINEMATICS A/B. Sub-split verified via kit color/helmet.
Race setup: ~2 min track, host gets 40 s head start.
Race, mostly host POV/chase cam on a rental bike. Asa catches host ~9:03 (543 s). Low value for side-on bike keypoints; possible Asa appearance near end.
